title.from: Shorten the standard issue-ID hash prefix from 6 to 5 characters
title.to: Dynamic short issue IDs: default 4-character hash prefix, widened only on collision

description.from:
Change the standard way Kanbus abbreviates an issue's hash prefix in the Kanbus interface (CLI and console). Short IDs currently show 6 characters of the hash (for example kbs-60bf38). Make the standard 5 characters instead (for example kbs-60bf3).

Why 5:
- 4 characters carries a remote but real chance of collisions, which could confuse two different issues.
- 5 balances that collision risk against cognitive load for people reading the UI, and against token cost for agents doing the work. Every character removed cuts noise and token usage.

Scope: Kanbus's own issue-ID display and abbreviation (CLI output, console, and anywhere a short ID is generated or shown), plus unique-prefix lookups, which keep working. This is not about GitHub's commit-hash display.

Open considerations for planning: how existing 6-character references in comments, commits and docs keep resolving, and what to do when a 5-character prefix is ambiguous (fall back to a longer prefix).
description.to:
Change how Kanbus abbreviates an issue's hash prefix for display (CLI and console). Short IDs currently show 6 characters (for example kbs-60bf38).

New design: a dynamic prefix length.
- By default, show 4 characters of the hash in short IDs (for example kbs-60bf).
- Detect collisions in context. When rendering a set of issues (for example the output of kbs list), if two or more issues in that set share the same first 4 characters, widen the displayed prefix for that list or session only. Add characters as needed until every displayed ID in that context is unique.
- The full original ID is always kept. This changes only how much of the ID is shown in a given context, never the stored ID.
- Unique-prefix lookups (kbs show <prefix>, --parent <prefix>, and so on) keep working, and existing longer references in comments, commits and docs still resolve.

Why:
- 4 characters saves tokens for agents and cuts visual noise for people reading the UI.
- Collisions at 4 characters are rare.
- When a collision does happen, the extra characters are paid only in the context where it occurs, not across every ID everywhere.

Out of scope: GitHub's commit-hash display.
